units.characteristics: the perception of futility; weariness; the insatiable eye/ear; oblivion
units.gist: the VANITY FRAME (arena for the whole book) - endless cycles that never arrive, 'all things are full of weariness', 'the eye is not satisfied with seeing nor the ear filled with hearing', and no remembrance of former things - the self set against a wearying, forgetting world

units.characteristics: the searching self (heart applied to seek out); the unhappy business
units.gist: 'I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom all that is done' - the seeking heart set in motion (recurs 1:17, 2:3, 7:25, 8:16); it finds an 'unhappy business' and what is crooked it cannot make straight

units.characteristics: knowing as grief; the heart's great experience of wisdom
units.gist: GEM - the heart that acquired great wisdom finds it 'a striving after wind'; 'in much wisdom is much vexation, and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow' - understanding itself deepens grief

units.characteristics: the self-experimenting, appetite-indulging heart; pleasure tested and found empty
units.gist: the great experiment - 'I will test you with pleasure'; building, gardens, treasure, 'whatever my eyes desired I did not keep from them, I kept my heart from no pleasure'; the heart found pleasure in toil, yet 'all was vanity' - desire fully indulged, still hollow

units.characteristics: the hatred of life; the leveling of the wise and the fool
units.gist: wisdom exceeds folly as light exceeds darkness, yet 'the same event happens to all' and both are forgotten; 'so I hated life, because what is done under the sun was grievous to me' - despair born of death's leveling

units.characteristics: the restless, despairing heart over toil
units.gist: 'I hated all my toil' - it must be left to another who may be a fool; the heart 'gave up to despair'; 'even in the night his heart does not rest' - the sleepless anxiety of labour without lasting gain

units.characteristics: joy/enjoyment as the gift of God (the recurring refrain)
units.gist: THE JOY REFRAIN (first sounding; recurs 3:12-13, 3:22, 5:18-20, 8:15, 9:7-10, 11:7-9) - 'nothing better than to eat and drink and find enjoyment in his toil - this is from the hand of God'; joy given to the one who pleases him

units.characteristics: the appointed rhythms of the affections; a time for everything
units.gist: the seasons poem - weep/laugh, mourn/dance, love/hate, embrace/refrain, seek/lose, keep silence/speak; the inner life's emotions read as timed, seasonal, not self-willed but appointed

units.characteristics: eternity set in the heart; the God-given limit of knowing; joy and fear
units.gist: GEM - 'he has put eternity into man's heart, yet so that he cannot find out what God has done'; the ache of a heart made for the eternal but fenced from full sight; joy and doing good as gift; God's work endures 'so that people fear before him'

units.characteristics: the self facing judgment and its own creatureliness (as beast/dust)
units.gist: God will judge the righteous and wicked; man tested to 'see that they themselves are but beasts', the same breath, all to dust; 'who knows whether the spirit of man goes upward?'; the man told to rejoice in his work as his lot

units.characteristics: the tears of the oppressed with no comforter; the observer's grief
units.gist: 'the tears of the oppressed, and they had no one to comfort them' (twice) - the ache of uncomforted suffering; so bitter the observer counts the dead, even the never-born, more fortunate

units.characteristics: envy-driven toil vs the quiet handful (contentment)
units.gist: 'all toil and skill in work come from a man's envy of his neighbor' - achievement rooted in rivalry; against it 'better is a handful of quietness than two hands full of toil' - restful sufficiency over striving

units.characteristics: the insatiable, isolated toiler
units.gist: the man alone, no son or brother, 'his eyes are never satisfied with riches' (the never-satisfied thread), toiling and 'depriving myself of pleasure' for no one - endless accumulation emptied of a why

units.characteristics: the self's need of another; companionship against aloneness
units.gist: 'two are better than one' - if they fall one lifts the other, they keep warm, 'woe to him who is alone'; a threefold cord not quickly broken - the self held up by bond, exposed in isolation

units.characteristics: the un-teachable old king; the fickle favour of the crowd
units.gist: the poor wise youth better than 'an old and foolish king who no longer knew how to take advice' - unteachability as ruin; and the crowd who follow the new then 'will not rejoice in him' - favour that does not last

units.characteristics: reverent restraint before God; the guarded mouth and few words
units.gist: 'guard your steps... let your words be few, for God is in heaven and you are on earth'; do not let the mouth run ahead in rash vows; 'God is the one you must fear' - awe expressed as restraint of speech and heart

units.characteristics: the oppression of the poor observed; tiers of watching power
units.gist: seeing the poor oppressed and justice violated, 'do not be amazed' - the hierarchy where each official is watched by a higher; the observer steadied against outrage at a rigged order

units.characteristics: the money-lover never satisfied; riches held to one's own hurt
units.gist: 'he who loves money will not be satisfied with money' (never-satisfied thread); the full stomach that cannot sleep; riches 'kept to his hurt' then lost, leaving nothing in hand; 'all his days he eats in darkness, in much vexation and sickness and anger'

units.characteristics: joy/enjoyment as the gift of God (refrain); the occupied heart
units.gist: THE JOY REFRAIN - 'eat and drink and find enjoyment in all the toil'; the one given wealth AND 'power to enjoy them' and 'to accept his lot' - 'he will not much remember the days of his life because God keeps him occupied with joy in his heart'

units.characteristics: the un-enjoying soul; wealth without the power to enjoy it
units.gist: GEM - a man given everything he desires 'yet God does not give him power to enjoy them'; 'his soul is not satisfied with life's good things'; the enjoyment-less rich man worse off than a stillborn - the tragedy of appetite that cannot land on rest

units.characteristics: the never-satisfied appetite vs the sight of the eyes
units.gist: 'all the toil of man is for his mouth, yet his appetite is not satisfied' (never-satisfied thread); 'better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the appetite' - contentment with what is present over the roaming of desire

units.characteristics: the smallness and ignorance of man; life as a passing shadow
units.gist: man 'not able to dispute with one stronger than he'; 'who knows what is good for man... which he passes like a shadow?' - the self dwarfed, not knowing its own good, unable to see beyond itself

units.characteristics: grief as formative; the heart made glad by sorrow
units.gist: GEM - 'the day of death better than the day of birth'; the house of mourning better than feasting; 'sorrow is better than laughter, for by sadness of face the heart is made glad'; 'the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning' - grief that ripens the interior

units.characteristics: the corrupted heart; patience vs pride; anger lodging in the fool
units.gist: oppression 'drives the wise into madness, and a bribe corrupts the heart'; 'the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit'; 'be not quick in your spirit to become angry, for anger lodges in the heart of fools'; nostalgia for former days 'not from wisdom'

units.characteristics: the sheltering strength of wisdom; joy and consideration held together
units.gist: wisdom a protection like money that 'preserves the life of him who has it'; consider God's work (who can straighten what he made crooked); 'in the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider' - the two-handed posture toward providence

units.characteristics: the fear of God as the balance between extremes
units.gist: seeing the righteous perish and the wicked prolong, 'be not overly righteous... be not overly wicked'; 'the one who fears God shall come out from both of them' - fear of God as the steadying mean, not moral over-reach

units.characteristics: self-knowledge of one's own sin; the heart that has also cursed
units.gist: GEM - 'there is not a righteous man on earth who does good and never sins'; do not take to heart all people say, 'for your heart knows that many times you yourself have cursed others' - honesty about one's own guilt disarms wounded pride

units.characteristics: the seeking heart reaching its limit; wisdom far off
units.gist: 'I turned my heart to know and to search out and to seek wisdom and the scheme of things' (the seeking-heart thread from 1:13); yet 'it was far from me... deep, very deep; who can find it out?' - the searching self meeting the wall of the unknowable

units.characteristics: the ensnaring heart; man made upright but seeking many schemes
units.gist: GEM - the woman 'whose heart is snares and nets'; the soul 'sought repeatedly, but I have not found'; and the conclusion, 'God made man upright, but they have sought out many schemes' - the crooked-seeking bent laid over an original uprightness

units.characteristics: wisdom shining in the face; the wise heart that knows the time
units.gist: 'a man's wisdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed' - the interior legible outwardly; 'the wise heart will know the proper time and the just way'; yet no man 'has power to retain the spirit, or power over the day of death'

units.characteristics: the heart emboldened to evil by delayed justice; fear of God as the true reckoning
units.gist: GEM - 'because the sentence against an evil deed is not executed speedily, the heart of the children of man is fully set to do evil'; yet 'it will be well with those who fear God, because they fear before him' - delay breeds the daring evil heart; fear holds the long view

units.characteristics: joy commended amid unjust reversals (refrain); the sleepless seeking mind
units.gist: the vanity of the just treated as wicked and vice versa; still 'I commend joy' (THE JOY REFRAIN) - eat, drink, be joyful through the days God gives; and the applied heart that lets the eyes 'see no sleep' still 'cannot find out the work of God'

units.characteristics: the passions that perish at death; hearts full of evil yet the living have hope
units.gist: GEM - all in God's hand, but 'whether it is love or hate, man does not know'; the same event to all; 'the hearts of the children of man are full of evil and madness'; yet 'he who is joined with all the living has hope', while the dead's 'love and hate and envy have already perished'

units.characteristics: joy as the approved life (refrain); whole-hearted action while there is time
units.gist: THE JOY REFRAIN (fullest) - 'eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart, for God has already approved what you do'; enjoy life with the wife you love; 'whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might' - joy plus wholehearted engagement against the coming silence

units.characteristics: the ignorance of one's own time; the self snared unawares
units.gist: the race not to the swift; 'time and chance happen to them all'; 'man does not know his time' - like fish and birds 'snared at an evil time, when it suddenly falls upon them' - the self blind to when its hour comes

units.characteristics: the unregarded wisdom; the wise man forgotten
units.gist: the poor wise man who 'by his wisdom delivered the city', 'yet no one remembered that poor man' (the oblivion thread from 1:11, 2:16); 'wisdom is better than might', though 'the poor man's wisdom is despised and his words are not heard'

units.characteristics: the heart's inclination; a little folly outweighing much wisdom
units.gist: 'a wise man's heart inclines him to the right, but a fool's heart to the left' - the interior lean that governs the walk; and how 'a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor', the fool advertising his lack to everyone

units.characteristics: calmness laying anger to rest; the disordered order observed
units.gist: 'if the anger of the ruler rises against you, do not leave your place, for calmness will lay great offenses to rest' - composure that defuses wrath; then the upside-down world seen (folly in high places, slaves on horses) without the self being unsettled

units.characteristics: the self endangered by its own labour; wisdom as the edge
units.gist: he who digs a pit falls in, who breaks a wall is bitten, who quarries and splits is hurt; but 'wisdom helps one to succeed' - skill/forethought sparing the strength that folly squanders

units.characteristics: speech that reveals and consumes the fool
units.gist: the speech-legibility thread - 'the words of a wise man's mouth win him favor, but the lips of a fool consume him'; his talk begins in foolishness, ends in 'evil madness'; 'a fool multiplies words' - the mouth exposing the interior

units.characteristics: the inner thought that leaks; even in thought do not curse
units.gist: GEM - sloth that lets the house decay; then 'even in your thoughts, do not curse the king... for a bird of the air will carry your voice' - the private inner word treated as if it escapes; the interior is not truly hidden

units.characteristics: the venturing self acting amid uncertainty
units.gist: 'cast your bread upon the waters'; give a portion to seven or eight 'for you know not what disaster may happen'; he who over-watches the wind never sows; sow morning and evening 'for you do not know which will prosper' - acting faithfully without control of the outcome

units.characteristics: rejoicing in life while remembering the darkness (refrain + memento mori)
units.gist: THE JOY REFRAIN turned toward the young - 'light is sweet'; 'if a person lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember that the days of darkness will be many' - joy held together with the memory of death

units.characteristics: the free yet accountable heart; removing vexation
units.gist: GEM - 'rejoice, O young man... walk in the ways of your heart and the sight of your eyes; but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment'; 'remove vexation from your heart, and put away pain from your body' - freedom and accountability held in one breath

units.characteristics: remember your Creator before decline; desire fails; the spirit returns
units.gist: GEM - 'remember also your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come'; the allegory of the failing body; 'desire fails, because man is going to his eternal home'; 'the dust returns to the earth... and the spirit returns to God who gave it'; vanity of vanities

units.characteristics: the teaching self; words of delight and truth; study as weariness
units.gist: the Preacher 'sought to find words of delight, and uprightly he wrote words of truth'; the words of the wise 'like goads... given by one Shepherd'; and the caution - 'much study is a weariness of the flesh'

units.characteristics: the summation - fear God; the whole duty; every deed to judgment
units.gist: THE CONCLUSION - 'the end of the matter; all has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of man'; 'God will bring every deed into judgment, with every secret thing' - fear of God as the resolving centre of the whole search
